prompt: Match each Flux controller to its job.

pairs.right: Fetches a repository into an artifact
Builds a path and applies it
Sends events out, takes webhooks in

prompt: What is the artifact the source controller produces?

choices.text: The files at one revision, compressed
choices.why: Right. Other controllers download it instead of cloning Git themselves.

choices.text: The list of objects already applied
choices.why: That is in the Kustomization's status.

choices.text: A container image of the repository
choices.why: It is a tarball served inside the cluster, not an image.

choices.text: A signed commit
choices.why: Signing is a separate matter, in lesson 8.

prompt: Who decides what a person may do with Flux?

choices.text: Gitea's branch protection
choices.why: That governs what reaches main, not who may suspend a Kustomization.

choices.text: Kubernetes' own permissions
choices.why: Right. Flux has no users of its own; its objects are governed like any others.

choices.text: Flux's API server and its roles
choices.why: Flux has no API server; that is Argo CD's model.

choices.text: The flux command's login
choices.why: There is nothing to log in to.

prompt: Flux's resource that builds a path with Kustomize and applies it is called a ___, like Kustomize's own file.
Why is the root Application deleted before the others?

choices.text: Because deleting it deletes staging
choices.why: These Applications have no cascade finalizer, so staging stays.

choices.text: So nothing recreates the others
choices.why: Right. The root applies the others from Git, and would put them back.

choices.text: Because the root holds the cluster's credentials
choices.why: The controller holds those; the root is an Application like any other.

choices.text: Because Kubernetes refuses to delete children first
choices.why: Kubernetes deletes them in any order.

prompt: Why remove the argocd account's access to fleet the day Argo CD goes?

choices.text: Flux refuses to start while it exists
choices.why: Flux knows nothing about other accounts.

choices.text: Forgotten keys get used unnoticed
choices.why: Right. Retired systems' keys are a classic way in.

choices.text: The token would expire and lock fleet
choices.why: An expired token locks nothing.

choices.text: Gitea charges for each collaborator
choices.why: Gitea charges nothing here.

prompt: Why does the argocd/ directory leave fleet once Argo CD is gone?

choices.text: Gitea refuses directories nobody reads
choices.why: Gitea stores whatever is committed.

choices.text: It holds the argocd token
choices.why: It holds Application manifests, no credentials.

choices.text: Flux would apply the Applications in it
choices.why: Flux applies clusters/lab, and the Application kind would not exist anyway.

choices.text: Unread descriptions go stale
choices.why: Right. It goes in the same pull request that brings Flux in.

prompt: What does flux check --pre do?

choices.text: Verifies the flux binary's checksum
choices.why: The checksum was checked with sha256sum.

choices.text: Installs Flux in a dry-run mode
choices.why: Nothing is installed.

choices.text: Reconciles every Kustomization once
choices.why: There are no Kustomizations yet.

choices.text: Checks the cluster first
choices.why: Right. Kubernetes version and kubectl access.

prompt: The flux account's token has one scope. Which?

choices.text: write:repository
choices.why: Flux never pushes in this course; the image automation of lesson 7 is where that changes.

choices.text: admin
choices.why: No machine account gets admin.

choices.text: read:repository
choices.why: Right. Flux only fetches fleet.

choices.text: write:user
choices.why: Flux has no business with user settings.

prompt: Why does the lesson not run flux bootstrap on fleet?

choices.text: flux bootstrap does not support Gitea
choices.why: It has a gitea subcommand; the rule is the obstacle.

choices.text: It would install Argo CD again
choices.why: bootstrap installs only Flux.

choices.text: It pushes to main
choices.why: Right. So its three steps are done by hand, and the commit goes through a pull request.

choices.text: It needs a cloud account
choices.why: It needs a Git server, which Gitea is.

prompt: Order the three bootstrap steps after the merge.
trap: The Secret needs the flux-system namespace, which the components create, and the sync needs the Secret.

prompt: After the bootstrap, how is Flux itself upgraded?

choices.text: kubectl apply of the new release by hand
choices.why: Same as flux install: drift from Git.

choices.text: flux install against the cluster
choices.why: That would change the cluster behind Git's back, and the next reconciliation would undo it.

choices.text: It upgrades itself to the latest release
choices.why: Nothing in Flux upgrades on its own; the version is pinned in the file.

choices.text: A pull request that changes gotk-components.yaml
choices.why: Right. The flux-system Kustomization applies clusters/lab, Flux's own manifests included.

prompt: What does wait: true change about when the staging Kustomization is ready?

choices.text: It waits ten minutes before applying
choices.why: That is the interval, a different field.

choices.text: Ready means the pods are ready
choices.why: Right. Sync and health, folded into one answer.

choices.text: It waits for a person to approve each apply
choices.why: Approval happened in the pull request, before Git.

choices.text: It waits for the webhook
choices.why: The webhook triggers a fetch; wait is about health.

prompt: Someone scales staging to six by hand. With Flux as configured here, how long can that last?

choices.text: For ever, because Flux ignores replicas
choices.why: Nothing told Flux to ignore replicas.

choices.text: Up to ten minutes
choices.why: Right. The kustomize controller applies on its interval and does not watch.

choices.text: Until the next commit to fleet
choices.why: A commit triggers a fetch and a reconciliation, but so does the interval.

choices.text: A few seconds, like Argo CD's selfHeal
choices.why: That is Argo CD's watched model.

prompt: flux reconcile kustomization staging ___ makes the source controller fetch first, so the newest commit is used.
Why not set every Kustomization's interval to ten seconds?

choices.text: Shorter intervals disable pruning
choices.why: Pruning works at any interval.

choices.text: Flux refuses intervals under a minute
choices.why: It accepts them; the cost is the reason not to.

choices.text: Each run applies the whole path
choices.why: Right. Cheap for three objects, not for a thousand.

choices.text: Gitea would block the fetches
choices.why: The Kustomization interval does not fetch from Gitea at all.

prompt: What makes flux suspend different from the pause lesson 2 ruled out?

choices.text: It reverts every manual change when resumed
choices.why: Resume reconciles, which does put Git back, but that is not what makes it different.

choices.text: It is recorded in the object
choices.why: Right. SUSPENDED True is in the Kustomization's spec, visible to every query and alert.

choices.text: It needs an approved pull request
choices.why: It is a command against the cluster, which is why it must stay short.

choices.text: It also stops people from using kubectl
choices.why: Suspend stops Flux, not people.

prompt: While staging was suspended, a change was merged. What did Flux do?

choices.text: Neither fetched nor applied it
choices.why: The GitRepository is not suspended and kept fetching.

choices.text: Applied it, because suspend only stops pruning
choices.why: Suspend stops reconciliation entirely.

choices.text: Fetched the commit and did not apply it
choices.why: Right. The source moved on; the Kustomization stayed on the old revision.

choices.text: Rejected the merge in Gitea
choices.why: Flux never talks to Gitea's merge.

prompt: Why is the Receiver of type github when the Git server is Gitea?

choices.text: The webhook goes through GitHub first
choices.why: It goes straight from Gitea to the node.

choices.text: type is only a label and is not checked
choices.why: It decides how the request is verified.

choices.text: Gitea signs webhooks the way GitHub does
choices.why: Right. An HMAC of the body in X-Hub-Signature-256, which the GitHub receiver checks.

choices.text: Flux has no receiver for anything but GitHub
choices.why: It has several; github is the one whose signature Gitea speaks.

prompt: Why does Gitea refuse to call private addresses unless told otherwise?

choices.text: Webhooks to private addresses are not signed
choices.why: The signature is the same either way.

choices.text: Private addresses cannot receive HTTP
choices.why: They receive it fine, as the node did.

choices.text: Webhooks could probe internal networks
choices.why: Right. Without the limit, anybody who can add a webhook could reach the server's internal network.

choices.text: Flux's receiver only listens on public addresses
choices.why: It listened on a NodePort of a private node.

prompt: With the webhook working, why keep the GitRepository's one-minute interval?

choices.text: As a safety net for a webhook that was lost
choices.why: Right. A missed call is caught by the next interval.

choices.text: The webhook only works between intervals
choices.why: It works at any time.

choices.text: The interval signs the webhook
choices.why: Signing uses the shared secret.

choices.text: Flux refuses a source with no interval
choices.why: The reason is the lost webhook, not a rule.

prompt: On which NodePort does Gitea reach Flux's receiver in this lab?
A team insists that a manual change in production be reverted within seconds, always. Which difference matters?

choices.text: Watching versus an interval
choices.why: Right. With Flux the worst case is the interval.

choices.text: Argo CD reads Git and Flux does not
choices.why: Both read Git.

choices.text: Flux has no notion of drift
choices.why: It corrects drift, on its interval.

choices.text: Flux prunes and Argo CD does not
choices.why: Both prune when told to.

prompt: How do the two tools differ in what they do with a Helm chart?

choices.text: Only Flux supports Helm
choices.why: Argo CD renders charts in its repo server.

choices.text: Both install Helm releases the same way
choices.why: Argo CD never creates a Helm release.

choices.text: Argo CD renders it to manifests; Flux installs a Helm release
choices.why: Right. With Flux, helm list shows the release; with Argo CD there is none.

choices.text: Only Argo CD supports Helm
choices.why: Flux has a helm controller.

prompt: Which reasons does the lesson give for choosing Argo CD? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: It decrypts SOPS files without add-ons
choices.why: That is Flux's argument.

choices.text: It reconciles on an interval rather than on events
choices.why: That describes Flux, not Argo CD.

choices.text: One installation serves many teams with different permissions
choices.why: Right. Projects and roles do that.

choices.text: People who do not live in a terminal need to see what is deployed
choices.why: Right. Its web interface is the shared picture.

prompt: A change does not arrive and the Kustomizations say READY True. What do you check first?

choices.text: Gitea's branch protection
choices.why: The change was merged; the question is whether Flux fetched it.

choices.text: flux get sources git
choices.why: Right. A source that cannot fetch leaves everything downstream on the last artifact, looking healthy.

choices.text: The pods in staging
choices.why: They run the last applied revision and look fine.

choices.text: flux check --pre
choices.why: That checks prerequisites, not a running source.

prompt: Why did the bad image show up as a failed Kustomization rather than only as a failing pod?

choices.text: Flux pulls the image itself before applying
choices.why: The node pulls images; Flux never does.

choices.text: The source controller could not fetch
choices.why: The source fetched fine; the apply's result was the problem.

choices.text: Because of wait: true
choices.why: Right. timeout waiting for, naming the Deployment and the revision.

choices.text: kubeconform rejected the tag
choices.why: kubeconform passed it, as in lesson 2.

prompt: Order what happens between a merge and new pods when the webhook works.
items: The source controller fetches the new commit
The kustomize controller applies the path
The Deployment rolls out new pods
trap: Fetching comes before applying, and the artifact is what connects the two.

prompt: A platform team runs Flux, and an application team wants Argo CD's interface for the same staging objects. What does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: Run both on staging and let selfHeal win
choices.why: They would overwrite each other's changes and annotations on every pass.

choices.text: Suspend Flux whenever Argo CD syncs
choices.why: A Kustomization suspended indefinitely is a cluster that stopped being GitOps.

choices.text: Separate objects for each tool
choices.why: Right. Two reconcilers on one object is two truths with machines fighting.

choices.text: Replace Git with Argo CD's interface
choices.why: The interface reads Git; it does not replace it.

prompt: Which Flux controller takes webhooks in from the Git server?

choices.text: The source controller
choices.why: It fetches; it does not listen for webhooks.

choices.text: The kustomize controller, through a Kustomization
choices.why: It applies artifacts; it does not listen.

choices.text: The notification controller
choices.why: Right. Through a Receiver.

choices.text: The helm controller
choices.why: It installs charts.

prompt: Where does Flux keep everything it knows?

choices.text: In the Git repository, beside the manifests
choices.why: Git holds the desired state, not Flux's observations.

choices.text: In the status of its Kubernetes objects
choices.why: Right. kubectl and flux read it from there.

choices.text: In its web interface
choices.why: It has no web interface.

choices.text: In a database of its own
choices.why: It has none.

prompt: Why did deleting the Applications leave staging's pods running?

choices.text: Pods cannot be deleted while running
choices.why: They can.

choices.text: Argo CD never deletes anything
choices.why: It prunes when told to.

choices.text: They were created without the cascade finalizer
choices.why: Right. Deleting them did not delete what they managed.

choices.text: Flux had already adopted the pods, so they stayed
choices.why: Flux was not installed yet.

prompt: What does flux check --pre ask before anything is installed?

choices.text: Whether fleet has a flux-system directory
choices.why: It does not look at Git.

choices.text: Whether the registry has Flux's images
choices.why: It does not check registries.

choices.text: Whether the cluster meets Flux's requirements
choices.why: Right. A recent enough Kubernetes, and a working kubectl.

choices.text: Whether Argo CD is removed
choices.why: It does not look for other agents.

prompt: Why is the fleet-auth Secret created by hand rather than committed?

choices.text: Flux cannot read Secrets from Git
choices.why: It applies Secrets like any object.

choices.text: Gitea refuses commits that contain a Secret of any kind
choices.why: Gitea does not inspect content.

choices.text: It holds Flux's token, which must not be in Git
choices.why: Right. Lesson 9 shows how it could be, encrypted.

choices.text: The token changes every minute
choices.why: It is a long-lived token.

prompt: With interval: 10m and no webhook, how many minutes at most does a manual change to staging survive?
What does the annotation kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/ssa: IfNotPresent do?

choices.text: Ignore one field during comparison, as Argo CD does
choices.why: That is Argo CD's ignoreDifferences.

choices.text: Skip the object during pruning only
choices.why: It changes applying, not just pruning.

choices.text: Apply the object with client-side apply
choices.why: It is about whether to apply at all.

choices.text: Create the object if missing, then never touch it
choices.why: Right. Coarser than ignoring one field.

prompt: Why is flux suspend not the same as stopping an agent on a laptop?

choices.text: It reverts the cluster to the last commit
choices.why: It applies nothing while suspended.

choices.text: It also stops the source controller from fetching anything new
choices.why: Sources still fetch.

choices.text: It expires on its own after an hour
choices.why: It lasts until resumed.

choices.text: The pause is written in the object, where everybody sees it
choices.why: Right. Alerts on Flux's status see it too.

prompt: Why must the webhook be signed?

choices.text: Gitea refuses to send webhooks that carry no signature at all
choices.why: Signing protects the receiver, not Gitea.

choices.text: The signature carries the commit
choices.why: The commit comes from the fetch.

choices.text: NodePort Services require it
choices.why: Services know nothing about signatures.

choices.text: Otherwise anybody who found the path could make Flux fetch
choices.why: Right. The secret lives in the cluster and in Gitea.

prompt: An organisation runs Argo CD and Flux. What must it never do?

choices.text: Run them in one cluster
choices.why: They can share a cluster on different objects.

choices.text: Use Helm with both
choices.why: Each handles charts its own way.

choices.text: Read different paths of the same repository
choices.why: Different paths of one repository are fine.

choices.text: Point both at the same objects
choices.why: Right. That is two truths fighting.
